assessment: The marking can remove the sole member of a complete candidate cover and produce a checked local failure. It can also remove every offered witness while alternatives remain in the cursor. Marked search therefore needs further enumeration or stronger cover evidence when a witness sample becomes too small.

next-step: Next, qualify possible-support dependency updates, retained candidate packets, reference counts, cursor archives and exact rollback, then global engine decisions. These local controls do not yet qualify a complete search trajectory or establish a speed benefit.
outcome: All \(23\) declared checks pass without skips. Seven query fixtures and six real cursor contexts distinguish complete covers from incomplete witness samples. No target search was performed.
scope-text: The same fixed original language and marking are used throughout. Every marked candidate is rebuilt and checked against all assigned points. The independently implemented original cover checker runs before the marked filter; real cursors retain their full original context, order and completion records.
